cards.title: Form a new Task Force
cards.text: Create a Task Force in a port (or at sea where an existing TF is present) by placing ship counters and up to one nuclear submarine into a free Task Force marker box.

cards.title: Move ships in a Task Force
cards.text: Move all ships in a TF together per the movement rules. Triggered by the SHIPS event from the Operations Points Record Track. Bad weather may halt surface movement.

cards.title: Fire missiles with a Task Force
cards.text: A Task Force attacks an eligible target with its ship-launched missiles. Black/yellow Soviet missiles need a Good detected TF target in the same zone; Poor detected targets may be attacked with a die roll.

cards.title: ASW in current zone (instead of moving)
cards.text: Instead of moving, a Task Force conducts Anti-Submarine Warfare in its current zone. The TF is automatically marked with Poor Detection (and may be upgraded to Good if it rolls two N1/N2 results).

cards.title: Prepare and resolve an Amphibious Landing
cards.text: Place a 'Landing' marker on a Task Force in a zone with an Amphibious Landing symbol. On its next chance to move, the TF resolves the landing instead of moving.

cards.title: Submarine move
cards.text: A submarine moves. Diesel submarines move 1 zone; nuclear submarines move 2 (or 3 on a Fast move). A moving Soviet SSBN may take one non-diesel submarine with it for no extra cost.

cards.title: Submarine moves then attacks a Task Force
cards.text: The submarine moves into a zone containing a detected enemy TF, then resolves a torpedo attack against it.

cards.title: Submarine attacks then moves
cards.text: The submarine resolves a torpedo attack against a detected TF in its current zone, then moves. Order matters: a sub that attacks first can disengage afterwards.

cards.title: Submarine moves and detects
cards.text: Move into a zone containing an enemy TF and attempt to detect it, applying or upgrading the Task Force's detection state.

cards.title: Submarine moves and goes On Patrol
cards.text: Move the submarine to a zone within its range, then place it 'On Patrol' so it can react to enemy units crossing into the zone for the remainder of the turn.

cards.title: Nuclear submarine missile attack
cards.text: A nuclear submarine launches a missile attack on a TF or facility in the same zone. The submarine must be in the same zone as the target (range expressed by movement, not missile reach).

cards.title: Multi-submarine missile coordination (2–3 subs)
cards.text: Two or three submarines all move to the same zone and resolve a single coordinated missile attack against one TF (7.4) or facility (7.5). Costs 1 OPS per participating submarine.

cards.title: Soviet SSBN takes a nuclear sub along
cards.text: When a Soviet SSBN moves, it may take one non-diesel submarine with it for no extra cost. Both subs are marked 'Spent' at the end. The escorting sub must be a nuclear attack submarine (not diesel, not an SSBN).

cards.title: Maritime Patrol flies and attacks or detects
cards.text: A Maritime Patrol unit flies within range and either attacks a known submarine via ASW or attempts to detect a Task Force. If a detection is placed or upgraded, the active player may take one further action against the same TF.

cards.title: MP or Fighter goes On Patrol
cards.text: An MP or Fighter unit moves to a zone within range and is placed 'On Patrol' so it can react later in the turn to enemy submarines, Task Forces, or air units crossing through.

cards.title: Air Strike
cards.text: Strike units fly a mission against a TF or facility. Fighters (escort) and Tankers (range extension) fly with the strike at no additional OPS cost.

cards.title: Return an On-Patrol Air Unit to base
cards.text: When it is your action, you may return 'Fresh' On-Patrol Air Units to base without spending OPS. The unit comes off On Patrol and becomes available for new actions.

cards.title: On-Patrol Fighter intercepts enemy air
cards.text: An On-Patrol Fighter (Interception mission) attacks enemy Air Units entering its zone without spending the unit. CAP fighters at base may also roll to defend against strikes on their base.

cards.title: On-Patrol MP attacks a crossing submarine
cards.text: An On-Patrol Maritime Patrol unit interrupts a moving enemy submarine in its zone and resolves an ASW attack against it.

cards.title: On-Patrol MP attempts Task Force detection
cards.text: An On-Patrol MP rolls to detect an enemy Task Force moving through its zone, potentially applying or upgrading detection.

cards.title: CAP attacks a strike on its base
cards.text: Every Fighter unit at base is always on CAP (even when Spent) and may roll to attack an enemy Air Strike attacking that base. Carrier-based fighters also defend Task Forces in their zone and adjacent land facilities.

cards.title: Repair a facility
cards.text: Remove a Hit from a damaged facility. If the removal would change the damage status (Heavy→Light, or Light→Undamaged), a die roll of 5+ is required, otherwise the action is wasted.

cards.title: Move ships between Task Forces
cards.text: Move any units from one Task Force to another existing Task Force(s) in the same zone. A unit moved from a detected force passes its detection status to the new TF unless the new TF already has a higher status.

cards.title: De-Mine a Port
cards.text: Roll a die requiring 5+ to reduce a minefield by one level (7+ if the facility is damaged). Heavy mining → Light mining → Unmined.

cards.title: Launch or move a RORSAT
cards.text: Launch a RORSAT from Tyuratam or move one already on the map to another zone. A roll of 1 destroys the satellite instead.

cards.title: NATO may attack Cuba
cards.text: NATO spends 6 OPS to attack Cuba. Soviet deploys the Cuban sub on 8+; NATO resolves up to 3 OPS of free missile attacks then an immediate strike with the four US 'Cuba' units. Cuba becomes active afterwards.

cards.title: Pass
cards.text: If you have fewer Operations Points than your opponent, you may pass. The opponent then plays the next action, after which you have another chance to act.

cards.title: Spend a First Strike Point (Soviet)
cards.text: The Soviet player may spend First Strike Points on a variety of options. Free to use when active; does not count as an action.

cards.title: Use a Soviet Spy (Soviet)
cards.text: The Soviet player may use a Soviet spy from the Spies Track for various effects. Free to use when active; spending one may reduce the Soviet Spy Infiltration Track.

cards.title: Play an event on one of your OPS cards
cards.text: When it is your action, you may play the (non-Reaction) event on one of the two cards you used for OPS this turn, paying the event's printed OPS cost.

cards.title: Play a hand card's event for +2 OPS
cards.text: Play the top (non-Reaction) event of a card from your hand by paying its printed event cost plus 2 additional OPS. The card is then discarded (or removed from play) per its instructions.

cards.title: Play a Reaction event from hand
cards.text: Play a card from your hand as a reaction to a specific game event. The card itself specifies when it is playable. After resolving, discard. If your hand drops below three cards, draw up to three.

cards.title: On-Patrol Submarine ASW vs moving TF
cards.text: An On-Patrol submarine may interrupt a Task Force entering its zone and roll to attack it.

cards.title: Hydrophone Barrier reaction
cards.text: When an enemy submarine crosses a Hydrophone Barrier (GIUK Gap, English Channel, Strait of Gibraltar), one Fresh or On-Patrol friendly unit in the entered or exited zone may interrupt to roll ASW. English Channel and Gibraltar also offer a permanent 2-die helo asset (unless Bad Weather).

cards.title: Draw a card (hand < 3)
cards.text: If you have fewer than three cards in your hand, draw a card.

cards.title: Soviet Spy for SSBN evasion
cards.text: During the NATO action, the Soviet player may spend a Soviet spy to evade SSBN-hunt resolution. May reduce the Soviet Spy Infiltration Track.
